### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/driver-turso`, touching **25** documentable anchor(s).

**8** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/index.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **13** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 246314dffef9af072b6172d0f1f9678fb7363dec` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e3beb770363735732f0f51dfb0ab28082b6a6e53` — the merge of head `5fb4b25b1218a23759a2d7d45e55bd5d553da899` into base `246314dffef9af072b6172d0f1f9678fb7363dec`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e3beb770363735732f0f51dfb0ab28082b6a6e53 && git checkout e3beb770363735732f0f51dfb0ab28082b6a6e53
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 246314dffef9af072b6172d0f1f9678fb7363dec 5fb4b25b1218a23759a2d7d45e55bd5d553da899 && git checkout -B drift-repro 246314dffef9af072b6172d0f1f9678fb7363dec && git merge --no-ff 5fb4b25b1218a23759a2d7d45e55bd5d553da899

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 246314dffef9af072b6172d0f1f9678fb7363dec
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 246314dffef9af072b6172d0f1f9678fb7363dec` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b6f40dc9564de59ef4962fbb4c9484cc07afa916`

The merge base with `origin/main` is `9d81af714`; the branch merged `main` at `3bf7a68ce`. The diff against it is 25 files, +1033/−115, as the PR states. Reviewed in the reviewer's own detached worktree at head, removed afterwards. Base-vs-head readings were taken with the two door files reverted to the merge base by blob and restored by blob.

### ① Derived judgments

- **A. Accept set: unchanged, RIGHT.** 9 door variants × `find` / `count` (18 cells) are refused `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 in every cell at base and at head. The four doors' trigger conditions are untouched. `Clause-②: no` holds.
- **B. The wire message at each converted driver-sql door.**
  - `'policy'` and unmarked are withheld: RIGHT.
    - The pin file is 34/34 at head.
    - The reviewer's own dump of unmarked wheres shows zero occurrences of the field, comparand or operator across 18 cells.
    - Measured through a real `ObjectQL` + `SqlDriver` under five hosts: no security plugin; a `plugin-security`-shaped merge with the door in the `'policy'` arm; the real `SecurityPlugin` in system context; the same in anonymous context; and a member where holding `{current_user_id}`. Every row answered `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 with zero leaks, and every secret appeared in the server log line.
  - `'author'` keeps today's text byte for byte: RIGHT. The base dump and head's author dump are identical in all 18 cells. A member's plain where under the real `SecurityPlugin` gets the full text.
  - The column door through a real CEL policy on a declared-but-dropped column is withheld; a member where naming the same column beside that policy is also withheld (the both-arms rule). RIGHT.
- **C. Mark resolution: RIGHT.**
  - The innermost mark wins, and the refusing arm decides. Both arm orders, nesting under `$or` / `$and` / `$not`, and the path-to-node index are sound.
  - Hunted disclosure paths: the thrown error's own keys are exactly `code` and `status` (no `details`, `constraint` or `cause`, and REST never relays `cause`). The wire carries no arm order, index, nesting, path or dialect text. The only per-door variant is the class statement, the contract's "which class fired", the same shape #8197 ships.
- **D. The Turso `RemoteTransport` twins: RIGHT.**
  - 29/29 pins at head, and 29/29 red with the file at base.
  - `TursoDriver.toRemoteFilter` rebuilds each node from `Object.entries`, so no mark reaches the transport in remote mode and every mark-reading refusal withholds there (code + pin).
  - The sink is wired to `logger.warn`.
  - The remote unresolvable column answers `[]`, untouched.
- **E. Public surface: RIGHT.** No export is added or removed. Two `protected` methods gain a trailing optional parameter, which is compatible and declared.
- **F. Caller populations that lose their own diagnostic at these four doors.**
  - Measured by this review: no security plugin, system context, anonymous, a where holding a placeholder token (rewritten before the merge), and Turso remote mode. The changeset and body state this cost truthfully.
  - **WRONG / undeclared:** an in-repo consumer in exactly this population, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-contains-filter.test.ts:309-310` (#5893 face 3: an unmarked `engine.find('sys_user', { where: { name: { $regex } } })` asserting `$regex` and `$icontains` in the message), is red at this head. Reproduced locally: `1 failed | 8 passed (9)`.
- **G. Suites in the reviewer's worktree:**
  - with the doors reverted: driver-sql 32 of 34 red (the 2 passes are author cases base satisfies by disclosing to all), and turso 29/29 red;
  - at head: driver-sql 2771 / 170 skipped, driver-turso 1473, sqlite-wasm 582, equal to the PR body.
- **H. CI at this head:** 34 runs.
  - **`Test Core` FAILURE** (`Test Core (6/6)`: `@objectstack/plugin-auth#test`, `auth-contains-filter.test.ts › [#5893] … refuses a bare $regex …, naming its replacement`, "expected 'A filter operator in this filter is R…' to contain '$regex'").
  - At the merge base, `Test Core (6/6)` is success, so the red is caused by this diff.
  - Every other required context is `success`.

### ② Semver level

`patch` for `@objectstack/driver-sql` and `@objectstack/driver-turso`, with `Clause-②: no`: RIGHT. The accept set does not move, message text is outside the published accept set, and no export changes. The closest precedent, #8197, shipped as a patch. driver-sqlite-wasm needs no entry (one `fixed` group; only a test file changed). Wording note: the changeset does not say that `SqliteWasmDriver` and Turso local mode inherit the change.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Changeset:** every sentence is TRUE, including the four door bullets, "reads the mark on the node it refused", the withheld and `'author'` semantics, the lookup rules, "What an unmarked caller loses" and its four measured cases, the member case, the remote-transport paragraph, "Not changed" and the engine-door disclaimer. The analytics HTTP half of "Measured on both faces" is UNMEASURED by this review; its code path is consistent.

**Shipped strings:** every sentence of the four driver-sql withheld messages and the five `[RemoteTransport]` messages is TRUE. None carries a tracker number.

**PR body:**
- TRUE: "Code and status are unchanged", "The set of refused filters is unchanged", the byte-identical author text, the per-door CRUD rows, the engine rows (the doors run before the merge on CRUD, and ignore the mark on the analytics-shaped tree), and the host × mark table rows measured.
- **FALSE by omission:** the Tests section presents the changed pins as complete while a dependent's pin on this exact wording (`plugin-auth` #5893 face 3) is red, and "Suites at head" does not list plugin-auth.

**The dev's open questions and out-of-scope findings, judged for truth:**
- The engine doors relay policy content on the analytics face and see no mark on CRUD hosts: **REAL** (measured; the ordering was verified in `engine.ts`).
- Eight more driver-sql doors relay on the CRUD face: **REAL**, all eight measured under a `'policy'`-marked arm through real `ObjectQL` + `SqlDriver`.
- The analytics caller-where non-boolean `$null` / `$exists` is answered and coerced: **REAL** by code reading (`filter-normalizer.ts` reads the flags by identity and lowers everything else to `IS NOT NULL`). The HTTP measurement is UNMEASURED here.
- Turso remote always withholds: **REAL**. driver-memory and driver-mongodb do not read the mark: TRUE (grep).

**Other flags:**
- `RemoteTransport.unsupportedOperator`'s `$between` arm still names its target. It is unreachable from a policy through `TursoDriver`, and was declared in the dev report but not in the PR body.
- The per-surface roster for compile faces 3, 4, 5 and half is in the dev report only.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-20020-refusal-doors-provenance`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Bvd69VPa6puiNzzPUroDBx`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

What must change:
1. `plugin-auth/src/auth-contains-filter.test.ts:309-310` is red at this head, so the required context `Test Core` is red for a reason in this diff. Resolve it in this PR and state the choice.
2. Declare the cost truthfully in the PR body: list `plugin-auth`, and any other dependent of `driver-sql` whose pins read door wording, among the suites run at head, and name the consumer pin that changed.

Isolated reviewer: a contract-review-tier subagent, fed only the card, the contract file, the PR and AGENTS.md; adopted by the seat.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5fb4b25b1218a23759a2d7d45e55bd5d553da899`

Second round, after FAIL 5823428898 at `b6f40dc95`. The merge base is `9d81af714`, and the whole diff is 26 files, +1096/−126. The patch round `b6f40dc95..5fb4b25b1` is exactly two files: the changeset (+3) and `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-contains-filter.test.ts` (+60/−11). No source moved: the blobs of `sql-driver.ts` and `remote-transport.ts` are identical at both commits.

Scope read:
- card #20020 and its comments, including amendment 5823437510 and the two `os-dev-report`s, read as claims;
- the PR body, diff, commits and check-runs, and the prior record;
- AGENTS.md, and the code at head.

Measured in the reviewer's own detached worktree at head, which was removed afterwards.

### ① Derived judgments

- **A. Prior must-fix 1, plugin-auth face 3 re-pinned: RIGHT.**
  - At head the file is 10/10.
  - The unmarked leg asserts `INVALID_FILTER`, 400 and the class statement `is RETIRED`. It asserts that `$regex` and `$icontains` are absent from the message, and that both are present in the spied driver log, which is the real `logWithheldFilterDiagnostic` sink. It is the production shape on this path, because no merge boundary sits between the facade and the driver.
  - The `'author'` leg is a real round trip through `markFilterSubtreeProvenance`.
  - **Ablation through dist:**
    - with `sql-driver.ts` at the merge-base blob and driver-sql rebuilt, face 3 gives `1 failed | 9 passed`: the unmarked leg is red and the author leg green. The driver-sql pin file control gives `32 failed | 2 passed`.
    - Restored by blob (HEAD `3caf969f6e`, porcelain empty), face 3 is 10/10 and the pin file 34/34.
- **B. Prior must-fix 2, the cost declaration and the consumer sweep: RIGHT.**
  - The old-wording sweep reproduces the dev's 101 files exactly; the positive control is `auth-contains-filter.test.ts` itself.
  - Outside the drivers, `packages/spec` and memory/mongo, 46 files were read at every hit line.
  - A trigger-token sweep covered 306 test files that import a SQL-family driver, 28 of them carrying a door token. An assertion-shaped grep gave 41 lines.
  - None of these pins the four doors' wording except plugin-auth's own file.
  - CI Test Core shards 1–6 are green; the 6/6 log shows plugin-auth at 114 files / 2440 tests.
  - The PR body now names plugin-auth, the changed pin, and the rest of shard 6/6.
- **C. The changeset delta: RIGHT.** `SqliteWasmDriver` and `TursoDriver` (local) both `extends SqlDriver`. The probe ran 8 door variants × `find` / `count` × 9 mark shapes = 144 cells per driver, on `SqlDriver`, `SqliteWasmDriver` and `TursoDriver(':memory:')`:
  - every cell is `INVALID_FILTER` / 400;
  - every non-author cell names no field, comparand, operator or path, and logs the secret;
  - every author cell carries the full text;
  - the 70 parity cells are byte-identical across the three drivers.

  "the same four doors answer the same way there" is TRUE.
- **D. Regression against the prior record's passes: RIGHT.**
  - The accept set: 432 of 432 cells are refused at head and at base. At base all 240 non-author cells leaked; at head, 0.
  - The five RemoteTransport twins: 29/29, and the blob is unchanged since the prior record.
  - Mark resolution in both arm orders and under `$not`: RIGHT.
  - The error's own keys are exactly `code,status` in all 432 cells.
  - The public surface is unchanged.
- **E. CI at this head:** 41 runs, 36 success, 5 skipped, 0 failures, and all seven required contexts are `success`. `mergeable_state` is `clean`.

### ② Semver level

`patch` for `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/driver-turso` and now `@objectstack/driver-sqlite-wasm`, with `Clause-②: no`: RIGHT. The accept set is measured unchanged and no export moved. The sqlite-wasm entry carries the inheritance sentence into that package's CHANGELOG. The three packages are one `fixed` group, and `Check Changeset` is `success`.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Changeset:** the added sentence is TRUE (measured in C), and every earlier sentence stays TRUE. The analytics HTTP half of "Measured on both faces" remains UNMEASURED by this review.

**PR body, the new sentences:**
- The consumer-pin paragraph is TRUE clause by clause.
- The sweep's conclusion is TRUE: 101 reproduced exactly; the dev's 19 and 311 are within the variance of the filter used (20 and 306 here).
- The patch-round suites (plugin-auth, service-storage, cloud-connection, plugin-dev, connector-mcp, hono, sqlite-wasm) are TRUE, each run here. The full driver-sql and driver-turso counts and the cli unit count are UNMEASURED this round; their sources are unchanged since round 1.
- "turbo without `--continue`" is TRUE (`ci.yml`), and so is the `example-embed-objectql` dependency claim.
- The #20039, #20040, stale-prose and engine-half C notes are TRUE.

**Carried from round 1, not verdict-moving:** the per-face compile-surface roster and the unreachable `$between` arm were in the dev report only. The seat has since put both in the PR body.

**Docs:** no hand-written `content/docs` page quotes the old door wording.
